newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee closes up on high money rates.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee closes up on high money rates.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed slightly stronger against the dollar on Tuesday as traders hurried to hold rupees in the wake of rising money rates, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 56.93 to the U.S. currency after opening at 57.01 despite relatively heavy buying of dollars in the market to cover imports, they said.
The Central Bank pushed the U.S. currency down by half a local cent and fixed buying and selling at 55.9251 and 57.0549, respectively.
"The rupee appreciated because of the money market," a Standard Chartered Bank dealer said. "Money rates were high today, and people were selling dollars to carry rupee plus positions."
The day's attention was focused on the money market with rates climbing to 25 percent at one time after opening at 20 percent.
Overnight call money closed at 22 percent, dealers said.
